title: REST: resources, verbs, status codes and versioning

videos.script: Every app on your phone is talking to a server right now. It asks a question, and a program on the other side answers. {{phone}} The rules for that conversation are an API. They say what may be asked, how to ask it, and what the answer looks like. {{contract}} This course is about writing those rules well. And then about deciding who is allowed to ask. {{halves}} It starts on a machine of your own. You build an Ubuntu machine on your computer, and type in a small API for a bookshop. It is called shelf. {{lab}} Then you take REST apart, piece by piece. Addresses that name things. Methods that promise something. Status codes a program can act on. {{rest}} And at the end, a second version of one resource, to see why the first one has to stay. {{versions}}
